The Instant Pot met my criteria of being multiple use so I decided to give it a try. It has quickly become one of my favorite kitchen tools and I use it often.

Instant Pot: The Pros

All Stainless Interior: Unlike most electric pressure cookers, the Instant Pot has a fully stainless-steel interior so this is the only part that touches the food. While parts of the exterior are plastic or other materials, these do not come in contact with the food and there is no teflon or non-stick surface.

Multi-Use: As a multi-use gadget it could conceivably replace a slow-cooker, rice-cooker, saute-pan, and steamer. I’ve even had friends tell me that they now use the Instant Pot so often that they rarely use their stove and oven. I certainly can’t see the Instant Pot replacing my oven and stove, but it definitely could if I ever needed it to if one of those appliances broke.

Replace the Slow Cooker: The Instant Pot has largely replaced our slow-cooker and I’m considering even getting rid of the Crockpot completely since the Instant Pot works more quickly and often provides better results. I could see an electric pressure cooker like this one being especially helpful for anyone with a small kitchen as it could replace several other kitchen appliances.

Time Saving: This is perhaps the biggest benefit I noticed right away with the Instant Pot. It can cook a slow-cooker recipe that takes 6-8 hours in just an hour and I can even prepare a roast for dinner in about 40 minutes. This is tremendously helpful on days that we aren’t home during the day and I need to prepare a meal quickly at night (or days that I forget to defrost food until the afternoon or to put food in the slow-cooker in the morning).

Good Price Point: While the Instant Pot does cost more than most single-use kitchen appliances like slow-cookers and rice-cookers, it is cost effective if you use it to replace one or more of these other gadgets. I found mine 50% off on sale here, and it has definitely already paid for itself in space and time savings.

Programmable: This is one advantage of the Instant Pot over regular pressure cookers and most slow-cookers. Since it cooks so quickly, I sometimes don’t need to start cooking a recipe as soon as I put it in the Instant Pot but I want to have it ready to go. The Instant Pot lets you program up to 24-hours in advance and has quite a few options pre-programmed for easy use.

Energy Efficient: Like a slow-cooker the heat source is electric and built in so it doesn’t require a separate gas or electric stove and is more energy efficient. Since it is self-regulated, it is also safer, and easier to use (in my opinion).

Easy to Clean: Since the cooking bowl is all stainless-steel it is easy to clean by hand and can even be placed in the dishwasher.

    Love, love my Instant Pot DUO60 even better than the Instant Pot Ultra!
    Reviewed in Canada on January 28, 2016
    Size: 6 QuartsStyle: Instant Pot
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.

    I'm thoroughly enjoying my Instant Pot. I got the IP, instead of other brands, because it has a stainless steel liner. And this model even has a special setting for yogurt, which also works perfectly.

    My original Instant Pot gave out 3 mos after the warranty ran out. (It just didn't heat any more, although the display worked fine.) After some correspondence with Customer Support, they replaced my original Instant Pot, and the new one was "Version 2" which is a considerable improvement on the original version, since this version "remembers" all my previous settings.

    There are 31 factory default settings, including number of minutes and temperature (as Sautee). All of these, except Rice, to the best of my knowledge can be modified to suit my personal use pattern. Thus the pot allows for 31 personalized "remembered" settings. This is much more than the new Instant Pot Ultra Electric Pressure Cooker, 6Qt 10-in-1, Stainless Steel (2017 Model) can do. (I recently bought the Ultra and decided it was much less convenient than the DUO, with fewer remembered setting. I will review it as well.)

    Here are the Factory Default Settings that can be adjusted (except the Rice setting):

    *IP DUO Factory Default Settings*

    Additionally all pressure settings have High/Low settings. Three settings are accessed with “Adjust” button. Defaults are indicated like *this* since I can't use bold:

    • Soup: Hi 20, *30*, 240 min

    • Meat: Hi *10*, 35, 45 min

    • Beans: Hi 10, *20*, 50

    • Poultry: Hi *6*, 15, 20

    • Slow: 4:00 Less, *Normal*, More

    • Rice: Lo *12* (Not adjustable0

    • Multi-Grain: Hi 20, *40*, 60

    • Porridge: Hi 5, *20*, 30

    • Steam: Hi 3, *10*, 15

    • Yogurt: Less 24:00, *Normal 22:00*, More /boil

    • Sautee: 30 min. Low, *Medium* or High Temp

    • Manual: Lo 1

    You can customize nearly everything. If you don't cook meat, for instance, you can program that button for something else. Ditto for beans or whatever.

    *To Reset to Factory Defaults*

    Hold “Adjust” for 3 seconds in “OFF” mode.

    And these are the DUO60 Preset Working Temperatures which you cannot change. (By contrast, you have customizable temperatures on the Instant Pot Ultra, but for that you give up about 20 of the presets and have to push, spin, push, spin, push, etc. each time you want to use a setting, rather than the one-time or up to three-time button push on the DUO, which is much faster.)

    • Yogurt Less (Jiu Niang, Natto) 86.8-93.2ºF

    • Yogurt Normal 96.8-109.4ºF

    • More/Pasteurize/Sterilize 180ºF

    • Keep Warm 145- 172ºF (Not adjustable)

    • Slow Cook Lo 180-190ºF

    • Slow Cook Med 190 – 200ºF

    • Slow Cook Hi 200 – 210ºF

    • Steam Setting 212ºF

    • Low Pressure 229-233ºF

    • High Pressure 269 -244ºF

    • Sautee Lo 275 – 302 ºF

    • Sautee med 220 - 349ºF

    • Sautee Hi 247-410ºF

    DUO60 Fully Automated Programs

    • Rice works like rice cooker, with cooking time dependent on amt of rice. Adjust key has no effect on the time, which shows up as 12 min.

    DUO60 Semi-Automatic Programs

    • Multi-grain “More” includes 45 min of warm-water soaking, 60 min pressure

    The newest Instant Pot DUO 6.00 I bought in October 2017 (third one, this one for a son and daughter-in-law) is the best one yet. Rather than a separate "Adjust" button for High/Med/Low, or the three time presets, it takes successive presses of the same button to cycle between the options. Fast! That's part of what puts the "instant" in the Instant Pot!
